html:
A thirty-year war in what is now southwestern Mauritania between Berber tribes led by the cleric Nasir al-Din and the Arab warrior tribes of the Banu Hassan, from 1644 to 1674.

Nasir al-Din called for a holy war to reform the region; the Hassan defeated his movement. The peace settled a social order that lasted into modern times: Hassan warrior tribes on top, Berber zawaya tribes as scholars and clerics, and tributaries and slaves below. Hassaniya Arabic replaced the Berber language. The emirates of Trarza, Brakna and Adrar that grew from it faced the French in the 19th century. See also the Almoravids and Berber history.
